papers.title_en: Your Voice Cloning System is Secretly a Voice Anonymizer
papers.authors: Romolo Muletta, Felix Matthias Saaro, Mark Cieliebak, Jan Deriu
papers.evidence: 通过伪说话人条件利用XTTSv2实现语音转换
papers.tldr: 语音匿名化旨在去除说话人身份信息同时保留内容和质量。本文发现XTTSv2语音克隆模型可无需重新训练直接用于匿名化，因为它能独立于说话人身份保留韵律结构。方法是通过伪说话人条件进行语音转换，并采用迭代优化策略平衡隐私与可用性。在七种欧洲语言上达到了接近最优的隐私性能，语音质量优于专用匿名化系统，且无需语言特定训练。
papers.abstract_en: Speaker anonymization suppresses speaker-identifying attributes from speech while preserving linguistic content and quality. We propose repurposing XTTSv2, a multilingual voice cloning model trained on 27k hours of speech, for speaker anonymization without retraining. Our key insight is that XTTSv2's voice cloning capabilities preserve prosodic structure independently of speaker identity, enabling voice conversion by conditioning on a pseudo-speaker. We introduce an iterative refinement strategy that balances privacy and utility by maximizing a harmonic mean of speaker dissimilarity and intelligibility. Evaluated on seven European languages across CommonVoice and Multilingual LibriSpeech, our system achieves near-optimal privacy (EER $\approx$ 0.49), competitive intelligibility, and substantially better speech quality than dedicated anonymization baselines, while requiring no language-specific training. We release the code here: https://github.com/rm00cr/coqui-tts.

papers.title_en: μNet: Ultra-Low-Memory and Low-Complexity Speech Enhancement for Embedded Digital Signal Processors
papers.authors: Shrishti Saha Shetu, Jose Miguel Martinez Aponte, Nagashree K. S. Rao, Sharvin Vittappan, Oliver Thiergart, Emanuël A. P. Habets
papers.evidence: 面向嵌入式音频设备的语音增强，属于语音音频核心主题。
papers.tldr: 语音增强在嵌入式DSP上受限于内存、计算量、延迟及整数运算支持，现有DNN方法未能同时满足这些要求。本文提出μNet，一种超低内存、低复杂度和低延迟的端到端DNN，仅需90KB静态内存和28MMACs计算量，支持最低4ms算法延迟。实验表明，其性能与同等复杂度的最先进方法相当，且兼容神经加速器和全整数运算，可在Cadence Tensilica HiFi 4/5等消费级DSP上部署。该工作为嵌入式语音增强提供了统一高效的实用解决方案。
papers.abstract_en: Speech enhancement on embedded digital signal processors (DSPs) imposes strict constraints on memory footprint, computational complexity, latency, and support for integer operations. Although recent DNN-based approaches have addressed these challenges individually, no unified framework in the literature simultaneously addresses all these requirements for practical deployment. In this work, we propose μNet, an ultra-low-memory, low-complexity, and low-latency end-to-end DNN model. The proposed method requires only $90$~KB of static memory and $28$~MMACs, while supporting an algorithmic latency as low as $4$~ms with performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods of similar complexity. Our experiments demonstrate that μNet is compatible with neural accelerators and supports full integer-arithmetic operations on consumer DSP platforms such as Cadence Tensilica HiFi 4/5.

papers.title_en: SlimDiffuSE: Towards Efficient Diffusion-Based Speech Enhancement using Slimmable Networks
papers.authors: Nagashree K. S. Rao, Shrishti Saha Shetu, Mohamed Elminshawi, Emanuël A. P. Habets, Andreas Brendel
papers.evidence: 基于可瘦身网络的扩散语音增强，属于语音与音频处理核心方向
papers.tldr: 扩散模型在语音增强领域取得领先性能，但其生成过程需要大量迭代且每步都使用大型网络，导致总体计算复杂度极高。为此，本文提出SlimDiffuSE，利用可瘦身网络在生成时按调度自适应调整宽度，并通过贪心搜索自动选择每步最优宽度。实验表明，该方案最多可减少87.5%的计算量，而PESQ、SI-SDR等客观指标几乎不下降。这项工作为扩散语音增强的实用化提供了高效且可扩展的解决方案。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion-based models are emerging in the speech enhancement domain and are achieving state-of-the-art performance across various benchmark datasets. A major downside of diffusion models is that data generation requires many evaluations of a typically large neural network, which results in high overall complexity. In this work, we propose a slimmable diffusion model that employs adaptive network widths throughout the data generation process to reduce computational cost. By using a greedy search algorithm to optimize the network width schedule, our method achieves performance comparable to baseline diffusion models with significantly reduced computational complexity. Notably, our approach reduces the computational complexity by up to $87.5\%$ without a significant drop in objective metrics, such as perceptual evaluation of speech quality (PESQ) and SI-SDR.

papers.title_en: Dual-Scale State-Space Modeling with Speaker-Wise Dynamic CRF for Speech Emotion Recognition in Conversation
papers.authors: Guan-Hua Wen, Kuan-Yu Chen, Hou-Chiang Tseng
papers.evidence: 基于双尺度状态空间建模与说话人动态条件随机场的对话语音情感识别
papers.tldr: 对话语音情感识别需同时处理跨说话人上下文影响与说话人内部情感演化。DSSM-CRF 利用双向状态空间模型在帧级和对话级编码融合的自监督语音表示，使话语同时捕捉局部韵律与全局上下文；解码时按说话人构建独立动态条件随机场链，转移得分由语料库级矩阵与上下文残差相加，并辅以目标监督情感变化但不参与推断。在 IEMOCAP 上达到 75.81% UA 和 74.90% WA，MELD 上达到 54.72% WA 和 49.31% WF1。消融对照证明两组件互补增益。
papers.abstract_en: Conversational speech emotion recognition must reconcile acoustic evidence across temporal scales with two interaction processes: cross-speaker contextual influence and within-speaker emotion evolution. We propose DSSM-CRF, an audio-only architecture that explicitly separates these processes. Bidirectional state-space models encode fused self-supervised speech representations at frame and dialogue scales, so each utterance representation captures local prosody and context from all speakers. The decoder then orders each speaker's utterances into an independent dynamic conditional random field chain. Consecutive utterances in a speaker's chain form a transition pair whose score combines a corpus-level transition matrix with a residual predicted from the two contextualized utterances. An auxiliary objective supervises whether each pair changes emotion but does not participate in Viterbi inference. Thus, interlocutor turns affect contextual emotion scores without being treated as transitions in another speaker's emotion trajectory. DSSM-CRF achieves 75.81% UA and 74.90% WA on IEMOCAP, and 54.72% WA and 49.31% WF1 on MELD. Matched controls demonstrate complementary gains from speaker-wise factorization and CRF modeling.

papers.title_en: CoSTALA: Compositional Spatio-Temporal Audio-Language Alignment via Multi-Grain Hierarchical Contrastive Learning
papers.authors: Peiwei Ren, Jinbo Hu, Fang Kang, Shan Liang, Yin Cao
papers.evidence: 基于多粒度层次对比学习的音频-文本对齐方法
papers.tldr: 传统音频语言模型难以处理日常空间中的多事件序列。CoSTALA提出从全局对齐转向细粒度时空推理，通过多粒度层次化对比学习显式建模时间依赖并锚定单个声学事件，在空间音频理解上取得显著提升，建立了新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Conventional audio language models (ALMs) have made significant progress in achieving alignment between auditory and textual representations, including recent explorations in spatial audio. However, in daily spatial scenarios, they still cannot effectively process multi-event audio sequences. Current approaches primarily rely on coarse-grained contrastive learning with global auditory and textual features, lacking the resolution to distinguish multiple sequential events. To overcome these limitations, we propose CoSTALA-a novel training paradigm that transitions from purely global alignment to fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning. By constructing a multi-granularity hierarchical loss function system, we achieve explicit modeling of temporal dependencies, and successfully anchors individual acoustic events to preserve their semantic purity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoSTALA significantly establish a powerful new framework for spatio-temporal audio understanding.

papers.title_en: REDnet: Recursive Encoder and Decoder for Speech Separation under Unknown Number of Speakers and Variable Number of Microphones
papers.evidence: 多说话人语音分离，属于语音与音频处理核心任务，契合综合语音音频主题。
papers.tldr: 语音分离通常假设说话人数已知且麦克风配置固定，但实际场景中两者常未知。提出RED递归编解码网络，解码器逐个检测并分离说话人，编码器递归融合多通道空间信息，实现单模型处理未知人数和可变麦克风数。在多个公共数据集上取得最优性能。
papers.abstract_en: We propose $\textit{recursive encoder and decoder}$ (RED) for building a single deep neural network (DNN) model that can separate multi-speaker mixtures containing unknown numbers of speakers and variable numbers of microphones arranged in an unknown geometry, a task that has not been studied yet. The decoder of RED recursively detects whether there are active speakers left and separates one speaker at a time. It is designed to be trained in an end-to-end fashion to improve separation performance. The encoder of RED recursively encodes each microphone channel of the input mixture, sequentially incorporating spatial cues. Combining both, the DNN can be trained to separate mixtures not only with unknown numbers of speakers but also with variable numbers of microphones, achieving state-of-the-art performance on multiple public datasets.

papers.title_en: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
papers.authors: Freeman Jiang, Ramon Sanabria, Soham Deshmukh, Bandhav Veluri, Simon Michael Vuch Williams, Elliott K. Suen, Garreth Lee, Kevin Yoonho Choi, Takuya Umeki, Riku Kubo, Sathvik Udupa, Chien-yu Huang, Shih-Yun Shan Kuan, Zhuoyan Tao, Satyapriya Krishna, Sefik Emre Eskimez, Yu Tsao, Hung-yi Lee, Shinji Watanabe
papers.evidence: 面向口语对话话轮转换的多领域基准与标注语料，属于语音/音频基准
papers.tldr: 自然对话中的话轮转换缺乏统一评估与多样化标注。提出TurnBench多领域基准，含30小时三重标注双人对话，覆盖6种交互风格，并标准化话轮结束与打断检测协议。对14个系统评测表明：话轮结束召回稳定，打断误报强依赖交互风格，且在填充词密集场景高发；人类在话轮结束前151毫秒开始回应，现有系统无法兼顾。已发布语料、104小时训练集、排行榜与可视化工具。
papers.abstract_en: Speakers in natural conversation take turns speaking and listening, deciding in real time when to take, hold, or yield the floor. However, turn-taking evaluation remains limited due to the lack of a consistent, linguistically grounded evaluation protocol and hand-annotated data covering diverse conversation types. To address this, we present TurnBench, a multi-domain benchmark that pairs a 30-hour, hand-labeled corpus of dyadic human conversation with a standardized evaluation protocol for end-of-turn and interruption detection. We set conversation type as a controllable experimental variable, covering six distinct interaction styles, and triple-annotate each conversation. Benchmarking 14 heterogeneous turn-taking systems, we find end-of-turn recall stable across types, while interruption false positives are strongly type-dependent and concentrated in backchannel-dense interaction styles. Although in smooth floor transfers human listeners begin speaking a median 151 ms before the current turn ends, no current system performs equivalently without incurring excessive false positives. We release our corpus, a 104-hour training set, and a public leaderboard with an interactive dataset viewer at https://turnbench.sesame.com

papers.title_en: A Reranker for Orchestrating Heterogeneous Speech and Text Retrievers
papers.evidence: 面向检索增强生成，协调异构语音与文本检索器的重排序器
papers.tldr: RAG系统虽能缓解大模型幻觉，但知识库常含语音与文本多模态数据，现有重排序研究不足。针对此，作者构建了包含查询、混合模态证据及相关性标注的数据集，并提出STeReO重排序器，统一聚合异构检索结果。实验证明其在单模态和混合模态场景下均能优选证据，显著提升下游问答性能，为多模态RAG提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have attracted significant interest for their ability to mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs). Although knowledge databases for RAG are increasingly diversifying to include various modalities such as speech and text, research on handling such multi-modal database scenarios remains limited. In this paper, we propose STeReO (Speech and Text Reranking Orchestrator), a reranker based on speech and text retrievers that aggregates disparate modality databases. To address the lack of specialized training data, we first curate a dataset comprising queries, mixed-modality evidence, and their corresponding relevance ranks. We then train the reranker and evaluate its effectiveness in both single-modality and mixed-modality scenarios. Our results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm excels at selecting the most relevant evidence, thereby significantly improving downstream question-answering performance.
